title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Distribution Centre Shipping Rule: Earliest Ship Date of a Sensor Delivery Under a Plan Member Waiver
content:
# Earliest ship date of a sensor delivery counted for a plan member waiver

Distribution Centre Shipping Rule, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program.

This rule sets the earliest permitted ship date of the next delivery of the CGM supply allowance (A4239) when Larkfield counts the units a plan member waiver must cover for that delivery on a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment. The delivery can ship today only when that date is not after today. The rule reads the latest refill shipment of the CGM supply allowance on the program, the carrier's proof of delivery for that refill, the newest written order of the item, and the customer's Insulin Pump Program enrollment: its status and the pump delivery date recorded on it.

## The rule

The ship-timing adjustment replaces the standard earliest permitted ship date, the first of these rules that applies governing:

1. When the customer's Insulin Pump Program is not closed and the pump delivery falls after the latest refill shipped and on or before the newest written order's date, the latest refill does not count and the delivery may ship today.
2. When the latest refill shipped by expedited shipping at no charge to the customer, because Larkfield delayed it, the earliest date is the tier's refill ship lead days, in calendar days, before its proof-of-delivery date, or its ship date when no proof of delivery is recorded, plus its supply days. The proof-of-delivery date is the delivery date on the carrier's proof of delivery for that refill.
3. Otherwise the standard earliest date applies: the tier's refill ship lead days, in calendar days, before the latest refill's ship date plus its supply days.

An Insulin Pump Program enrollment that is referral received, pending authorization, active or on hold is not closed. A customer with no Insulin Pump Program enrollment has no pump program that is open, so rule 1 cannot apply.

## Condition table

| Records show | Earliest permitted ship date |
|---|---|
| Insulin Pump Program not closed; pump delivered later than the latest refill's ship date and no later than the newest written order's date | today (the latest refill does not count) |
| Rule 1 does not apply; latest refill shipped by no-charge expedited shipping | proof-of-delivery date (its ship date when no proof of delivery is recorded) plus supply days, less the tier's refill ship lead days |
| Neither of the above | the standard earliest date: ship date plus supply days, less the tier's refill ship lead days |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

- A pump delivered on the very date of the newest written order satisfies "on or before" and rule 1 applies, provided the pump program is not closed.
- A pump delivered on the same date the latest refill shipped is not delivered after that refill, so rule 1 does not apply.
- A pump delivered after the latest refill but on an Insulin Pump Program that is now closed does not engage rule 1.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

Suppose the tier's refill ship lead days were 4. A hypothetical latest refill of 30 days of supply shipped on 1 March and was delivered on 6 March.

- Shipped by no-charge expedited shipping: 6 March plus 30 days is 5 April; 4 days before that is 1 April. On 31 March the delivery cannot yet ship; on 1 April it can.
- Shipped by no-charge expedited shipping with no proof of delivery recorded: the ship date stands, 1 March plus 30 days is 31 March; 4 days before that is 27 March.
- Shipped any other way: 1 March plus 30 days is 31 March; 4 days before that is 27 March.
- In either case, if an open Insulin Pump Program shows a pump delivered on 10 March and the newest written order of the CGM supply allowance is dated 12 March, the latest refill does not count and the delivery may ship today.
